claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 initially exists as a high-temperature single-phase BCC alloy.
Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed jointly by a composition-dependent thermodynamic driving force and kinetic suppression of transformation.
Composition and annealing temperature can affect B2/BCC decomposition and its length scale in related Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys.
Al-induced lattice distortions are a primary source of the thermodynamic driving force for phase separation in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Al promotes local ordering and a non-ideal mixing environment within the BCC matrix.
Sluggish atomic diffusion in the multicomponent matrix kinetically suppresses phase transformation at lower temperatures.
Increasing the isothermal treatment temperature past a critical threshold sufficiently enhances diffusion to overcome the kinetic barrier.
Once diffusion is sufficiently activated, the thermodynamic driving force causes ordering and nucleation of secondary phases.
Below the proposed critical temperature, Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 will remain single-phase BCC without secondary-phase precipitation.
Above the proposed critical temperature, detectable secondary phases, potentially an ordered B2 plus disordered BCC mixture, will form.
The controlled comparison varies isothermal temperature and holding time while keeping composition and other processing parameters constant.
Heat treatments should be conducted in inert atmosphere or vacuum over temperatures spanning the proposed activation threshold.
Compositional changes, oxidation, or irradiation may alter the relevant diffusion kinetics or thermodynamic parameters and invalidate the proposed behavior.
The critical temperature and relative magnitudes of the thermodynamic driving force and diffusion barrier are not known precisely.
Heating rate and holding time may change the quantitative transformation behavior.

Failure to observe secondary-phase formation after reaching temperatures at which diffusion is sufficiently enhanced, or failure of phase separation to correlate with the proposed threshold, would falsify the hypothesis.
